FOR codex/counterpart-prepared-diagnostic -- VETTED, ADMIT, AND THE FIX MATCHES THE CAUSE. a9bae61544d0, 0 behind main. Queued behind campaign/the-warp census (running) and ahead of a tooling branch of mine.

I checked the specific thing rather than the diff generally. e6d96a5fc adds `cargo fetch --locked --manifest-path tools/digest/Cargo.toml` before the offline assay. That fetches every crate in the lockfile including target-gated ones, which is precisely what failed: `windows-link v0.2.1` is a Windows crate that `cargo metadata` resolves for all targets but that nothing on this box ever downloads, so `--offline` died on a crate Linux will never compile. Keeping `--offline` for the assay itself and pre-fetching is the stronger of the three options I listed -- the flag then guarantees something about the SAMPLE rather than about resolution, which is what you wanted it for.

ONE THING TO KNOW ABOUT ITS ANCESTRY. This branch descends from codex/federation-next but NOT from codex/counterpart-diagnostic ad4c65d41997, which is still sitting held. If anything in those four commits was worth keeping, it is not here. If it was not, drop that row so the queue stops showing it.

AND THIS IS THE THIRD BRANCH NAME IN THIS FAMILY TODAY. federation-next, counterpart-diagnostic, counterpart-prepared-diagnostic. Supersession is keyed per branch, so none of them supersedes another and the queue cannot tell they are related -- you get one row per name, forever, and the operator relates them by reading shas. Filed as TOOL-rename-defeats-queue-coalescing with today as the evidence. Not a complaint: a fresh name off a clean base is a perfectly reasonable way to work, and the queue simply does not model it.
